Considering the submissions made by the learned counsels/ representative of the Parties, the Commission permitted the parties to have a joint discussion on the issue of reimbursement of costs incurred by the Petitioner in the developing/implementing its Transmission Project so far within three weeks and the Petitioner is directed to file the outcome of meeting within two weeks thereafter._ ” g) The aspect of compensation to the Petitioner by Respondent No. 9 has arisen in terms of the submissions of the latter and the claims submitted by the Petitioner. CTUIL has been directed to coordinate the matter inter se between the Petitioner and APDCL, and to this effect, CTUIL has convened tripartite meetings from time to time to assess and inform the respective positions taken by the Petitioner and APDCL. m) CTUIL mentioned that an Independent Engineer (IE) for the NERGS-I project was also appointed, and costs have been incurred towards the services of the IE. Minutes of the meeting, along with inputs provided by M/s NERGSTL and APDCL, shall be submitted to the Commission. On 27.10.2025, APDCL has filed a Reply, inter alia, submitting that APDCL’s liability is limited to reimbursement of actual costs incurred and does not extend to any other claim of the Petitioner. The compensation or reimbursement payable by APDCL to the Petitioner is strictly subject to the Commission's adjudication of their respective claims and contentions. CTUIL submitted that in its position of a neutral entity qua the Petitioner and Respondent No. 9, the claims of the Petitioner may be subject to the following: > _“ 4. In response, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner had participated in the joint meetings in good faith to arrive at an amicable outcome. However, the parties are clearly not in agreement and by placing reliance on a single sentence of Record of Proceedings dated 20.6.2025, the Respondents cannot alter the fact that there is no privity of contract between the Petitioner and APDCL. Further, on_ _5. However, the learned counsel for CTUIL as well as APDCL strongly opposed the Petitioner’s oral request to withdraw the Petition at this juncture of proceedings and sought liberty to file their objections after the Petitioner moves a formal application to this effect._ _“5. At the end, the learned counsel for the Respondents, APDCL and CTUIL, in the alternative, also suggested that if the Commission disposes the Petition as infructuous, and the Petitioner is granted liberty to institute a fresh Petition for the compensation towards cancellation of the project, the rights of the Respondents to rely and refer to the pleadings, proceedings, and the admissions made herein be also_ 32. In view of the above, the Commission, _vide_ Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 20.6.2025, permitted the parties to have a joint discussion on the issue of reimbursement of costs incurred by the Petitioner in developing/ implementing the Scheme so far and to file the outcome of the said meeting. Since the parties could not convene a joint meeting within the original timeframe, similar permission was again granted _vide_ Record of Proceedings dated 12.8.2025. Subsequent thereto, the parties have filed the outcome of the said meeting and several affidavits on the aspects of claims for compensation submitted by the Petitioner. Suffice it not that there has been no mutual settlement between the parties on this aspect. 34. We have considered the submissions made by the parties. While the parties have made elaborate submissions on whether or not the Petitioner can withdraw this Petition at this stage, we do not find it necessary to deal with them in great detail, as we find that the Petitioner’s plea presupposes that the present Petition has already been rendered infructuous. While it is true that the subsequent developments as put forth by the parties have been taken note of, and the proceedings that transpired thereafter also reflect that the Scheme is no longer needed, the Commission may still be required to rule on this aspect. The Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 20.6.2025 or for the subsequent hearings, which permitted the parties to have a joint discussion on the issue of reimbursement of costs incurred by the Petitioner in developing or implementing the Scheme so far, cannot substitute for a formal decision 37. Accordingly, we deemed it appropriate to grant liberty to the Petitioner to file a separate Petition in regard to its claims for compensation towards the cancellation of the Scheme, which shall be dealt with in accordance with the law. Further, keeping in view the request of the learned counsel for the Respondents, as made during the course of arguments on 18.3.2026, we also allow all the parties to refer to and rely upon the pleadings, proceedings, submissions and admissions, if any, forming part of the present Petition in accordance with law.
